newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM sees no threat from EC probe into BA-AMR deal.
newsitem.headline: KLM sees no threat from EC probe into BA-AMR deal.

text.p: European Commission objections to a proposed tie-up between British Airways and American Airlines pose no real threat to similar European-U.S alliances on the continent, outgoing KLM president Pieter Bouw said on Thursday.

Bouw said the probe instituted by the European Commission (EC) into the implications of the planned BA-AMR alliance for fair competition were highly unlikely to result in a veto of other transatlantic tie-ups now also under examination.
These include KLM's partnership with Northwest Airlines and the Lufthansa -SAS-United Airlines deal.

"Based on the principle of equal treatment, these arrangements must also be vetted by Brussels, but the KLM- Northwest alliance has existed for many years without being challenged," Bouw said ahead of a lunch with journalists.

The European Commission's reservations on the BA-AMR deal were not expected to affect continental tie-ups given the wide range of airline alternatives available to continental European consumers, he said.
Bouw added that he did not see the BA-AMR deal being scuppered despite the "legitimate questions" it raised regarding the dominant market position of the ensuing alliance.
"I cannot believe the alliance will not go ahead -- both airlines have done their homework," he said.

The European Commission is widely expected to order changes to the BA-AMR deal after commission sources said on Tuesday it had concluded that, as the deal now stands, it would harm competition, particularly between the United States and Britain.
Bouw, 55, announced at the presentation of KLM's annual results on Wednesday that he would step down as KLM president and chief executive officer in August.
